chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the performer of Tamattu' who could not find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'He should fast three days during the Hajj: one day before Tarwiyya, the day of Tarwiyya, and the day of Arafat.' I said, 'What if he misses that?' He said: 'He should take a pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasba (departure) and fast that day and the two days after it.' I said, 'What if his camel-herder does not wait for him? Can he fast them on the way?' He said: 'If he wishes, he can fast them on the way, and if he wishes, (he can fast them) when he returns to his family.'

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhul-Hijjah, day of departure to Mina
key_terms.جَمَّالُهُ: His camel-herder or guide accompanying him
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, day of Arafat
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْحَصْبَةِ: The night of departure from Mecca to Mina
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in between

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamatti' pilgrifm who cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the graduated fidya for a Mutamatti' pilgrim unable to afford the sacrificial animal, prioritizing fasting during the sacred days of Hajj (before Tarwiyya, on Tarwiyya, and on Arafat). It provides practical flexibility, allowing the expiation to be fulfilled on the day of departure (al-Hasba) if the primary days are missed, and permits the fasts to be performed either en route or after returning home, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease in ritual obligations. This ruling underscores the principle that financial incapacity allows for substitution with acts of worship, maintaining the integrity of the Hajj contract.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the performer of Tumatto, not finding a sacrificial animal. Heasws said: ‘He should Fast for three days during the Hajj – one day before Al-Tarwiyya (7th Zilhajj), and the day of Al-Tarwiyya (8th Zilhajj), and the day of Arafat (9th Zilhajj)’. I said, ‘Supposing he misses that’. Heasws said: ‘He should take a pre-dawn meal on the day of Al-Hasba (leaving) and he should Fast that day, and the two days after it’. I said, ‘Supposing his camelier does not stay for him, can he Fast these on the way?’ Heasws said: ‘If he so desires to, he can Fast these in the way, and if he so desires to, (or) when he returns to his family’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) and does not find offering-animal. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to fast three days in al-Hajj, one day before al-Tarwiyah (eight of Dhu al-Hajj ah), on the day of al-Tarwiyah and on the day of ‘Arafah.’ I then asked, ‘What is the rule if he misses it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He can eat food before dawn on the day of al-Hasabah, fast that day and two more days thereafter.’ I then asked, if camel man does not wait for him, can he fast on the way?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, if he likes he can fast on the way or when he returns home to his family.’”
